page: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by the ARM Neoverse-N2 architecture. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, clocked at 3.4 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 64 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache, alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration for AES. Paired with 512.0 GB of system memory, the instance delivers a generous 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation.

Local I/O performance is supported by 3,780 GB of attached NVMe SSD storage. In synthetic CPU benchmarks, the dedicated 64-core architecture yields top-tier multi-threaded performance, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 132,397.85 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 23,580.0. Memory throughput is equally robust, reaching 465.82 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 203.93 GB/sec for uncached writes. Conversely, single-core metrics fall into the average range, indicating that the instance prioritizes aggregate multi-core throughput and memory density over extreme single-threaded velocity.

The bundled high-capacity NVMe drive coupled with high memory bandwidth enables strong transactional performance, evidenced by top-tier PassMark database operation scores and 117.06 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. The server configuration delivers favorable cost efficiency for memory-heavy and disk-intensive deployments by utilizing energy-efficient ARM silicon instead of legacy x86 architectures.

Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is well-suited for large in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, distributed data processing, Clang compilation pipelines, and transactional database engines requiring high density and fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure E64pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine driven by a 64-core ARM Neoverse-N2 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz with dedicated physical cores and 128 MB L3 cache. It features 512.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, alongside 3,780 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. Benchmark results show top-tier multi-core compute capability, high uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 465 GB/sec, and strong database transaction execution, though single-core performance remains average. Without bundled GPUs, the server relies on efficient ARM execution to optimize resource density for scale-out architectures. The platform is designed for enterprise memory-intensive workloads, including large-scale Redis deployments, in-memory databases, high-throughput software compilation, and low-latency transactional database workloads.
